page-header.title: Page Header
page-header.purpose: The top of an app page: breadcrumbs or Back, the h1 title with its meta and actions, a description and optional section tabs.
use: The first element of every app page (list, detail, settings, overview).
Detail pages that need Back and section Tabs.
avoid: Section titles inside a page → Heading level 2.
Titles of dialogs, sheets and cards → their own title props.
Phone screens with a navigation bar → TopNavigation.
api: h1 = Heading/1 by default (Figma Master-Layout); headingLevel 2 = Heading/4 (the house ladder's h2) for a page title inside a tab or an embedded view under the app's h1 (the ladder row "Page title inside a tab")
Breadcrumbs for nested pages; a short eyebrow; Back = { label, onClick } with the chevron
status Badge / BadgeCounter; Tertiary buttons then at most one Primary
one or two sentences; Tabs for the page's sections

Start the page's sections at h2 Heading/4; a card right under the PageHeader takes an h2 in Heading/Subheading.

Keep the description to one or two sentences.

Don't use a heading level lower than 2 or skip the h1.
Don't repeat the title in the description.

Back is a button named after its destination; the chevron is decorative.

Action labels name the outcome ("Invite member", not "Add").

form.title: Form
form.purpose: Collect a set of values and submit them. Form is a <form noValidate> laid out as a Stack; useFormState holds values and errors and binds every Zen field in one spread; FormField labels custom controls, FormFieldset groups choices and FormActions is the footer row.
use: Anything that saves several values at once: sign-up, settings, create/edit, checkout.
A custom control that needs a label, help text and an error (Slider, ColorSelector, your own picker) → FormField.
A group of Checkbox or RadioButton rows with one legend and one error → FormFieldset (kind="radio" for radios).
The Cancel + submit footer of a page or card form → FormActions (it stacks on phones and can stick to the bottom).
avoid: A 3–8 field create/edit flow in an overlay → ModalForm (desktop) or BottomSheet (phone), with onSubmit={form.handleSubmit}.
Settings that apply at once → Toggle, outside any Form.
A single inline edit (rename a title) → HeadingField, saved on blur.
Filtering a list → Search and Chip filters; nothing to submit.
api: returns values · errors · touched · isSubmitting · isValid · isDirty · submitCount · submitError · setValue · setError · setTouched · reset · handleSubmit · fieldError
form.field · selectField · dateField · numberField · checkboxField · toggleField · radioField(name, value) · autocompleteField · richTextField
exactly the props each Zen field takes: <InputField label="Work email" {...form.field("email")} />

gap lg between groups (default); a failed submit focuses the first invalid field (an AutocompleteField: its first Error tag's Remove button, else Add Item — never a valid tag) and announces "N fields need attention"
<FormField label helpText error required optional labelTooltip labelAction>
passes id, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-invalid and aria-required to its one child
<FormFieldset legend kind helpText error required optional direction gap hideLegend>
kind: group · checkbox · radio (role=radiogroup) · toggle (rows md apart, full width)
align end (default) · start · between; form < 480px or breakpoint mobile → full-width lg buttons, Primary on top; sticky → pinned bar, Pale top line, safe-area padding
keyboard: Submit the form (through its type="submit" Button)
Focus moves to the first invalid field
Check a Checkbox · switch a Toggle
Move and select within a radio FormFieldset
do: Bind fields with the helpers ({...form.field("email")}, {...form.selectField("role")}, {...form.checkboxField("terms")}); each one matches its field's own change signature.
Show an error when the user leaves a field with a bad value or submits, and clear it as soon as the value is fixed (useFormState does both).
Write each error as the fix: "Enter a valid email address, like name@company.com".
Group related fields in a Stack gap md (or a Grid columns={{ mobile: 1, desktop: 2 }}); Form spaces the groups lg.

Give every FormFieldset a legend, and kind="radio" to a group of RadioButtons (harness: form-fieldset/needs-legend, form-fieldset/radio-kind).
Put field errors from the server on the field with setError; show a failed request (thrown by onSubmit, in submitError) in a Negative InlineMessage with a Try again action, keeping every value.
Show progress on the submit button while isSubmitting ("Saving…").
On a phone, use sticky FormActions so the main action stays above the home indicator while the fields scroll.
Mark the exception: when most fields are required, label only the optional ones (labelOptional / optional).

Using react-hook-form? Wrap each Zen field in its <Controller> and map value, the field's change callback (onValueChange(value) on every Zen field — or onChange(event) on the text fields — and onCheckedChange(checked) on Checkbox and Toggle), onBlur and error={fieldState.error?.message}; <Form onSubmit={handleSubmit(onValid)}> still focuses the first invalid field and announces the count.

Don't put Toggles in a Form that is saved later; use a Checkbox, and keep instant Toggles outside the Form (harness: form/toggle-outside-form).

Don't clear the fields after a failed submit, and don't use the placeholder as the label or for instructions.

A failed submit moves focus to the first invalid field (scrolled to the middle) and announces "N fields need attention" in a polite live region; handleSubmit also focuses when passed to ModalForm or a plain <form>.
Zen fields set aria-invalid and link their message with aria-describedby; FormField passes the same attributes to a custom control, which must put them on its focusable element.

Errors are Help-Text Negative (icon + text), never colour alone.

Submit labels name the outcome ("Create account", "Save changes", "Send invite"); progress labels end with an ellipsis ("Saving…").
Legends are short nouns or phrases ("Delivery", "Email me about").

Toggles apply at once, so they never wait for a Form's submit: use a Checkbox for values the submit saves, and keep instant Toggles outside the Form.
Every FormFieldset has a legend that names the group; screen readers read it before each option.

link.title: Link
link.purpose: Navigates to another page, section or site from inside text or next to it. It uses the Content/Hyperlink colours and takes the font of the text around it; actions on the page are Buttons.
use: Links inside running text: help copy, descriptions, empty states, inline messages.
Standalone links to a related page (“View all invoices”, a footer link).
Other sites (docs, status page) in a new tab with external.
Client-side routes through your router's link: as={RouterLink} to="/x".
avoid: An action on this page (save, open a dialog, delete) → Button (level="tertiary" or appearance="flat").
A whole row or tile that opens something → ListItem href or a clickable Card.
Moving between app sections → Sidebar, Tabs or Bottom Navigation.
The path of parent pages → Breadcrumbs.
api: hyperlink (default: Default, Pressed while pressed) · inherit (the surrounding text colour; underlined by default)
opt-in Hyperlink/Visited after the destination was visited (search results, docs)
hover (default; also on keyboard focus) · always (running text, inherit tone) · none (only where the context says it is a link)
target="_blank" + rel="noopener noreferrer" + icon-link-external-line + a hidden “(opens in a new tab)”
as={RouterLink} to="/x": every other prop and the ref are forwarded
renders a <button> without browser chrome (no fill, border, padding or margin; font, spacing and alignment inherited), so it looks exactly like the anchor link
put it inside Text or a line of copy; Link sets no font of its own
keyboard: Move to the next / previous link
Follow the link (external: in a new tab)
do: Write link text that names the destination and makes sense on its own (“Billing settings”, “Status page”) (harness: link/vague-text).
Underline links inside running text with underline="always", so they never rely on colour alone.
Open other sites with external: it adds the icon, the hidden “(opens in a new tab)” and rel="noopener noreferrer" (harness: link/new-tab-is-external).
Render client-side routes with as={RouterLink}; the router's own props (to, replace) are forwarded.
Place a Link inside a Text or a line of copy: it takes that text style and size.
Keep tone="inherit" links underlined (the default for inherit) in legal lines, captions and footers (harness: link/inherit-needs-underline).
Turn on visited only for content people scan repeatedly, such as search results and docs.
dont: Don't use a Link for an action on the page (open a dialog, delete, save); that is a Button (harness: link/needs-href).
Don't write “click here”, “here”, “read more” or “learn more” as the whole link text (harness: link/vague-text).
Don't open a new tab with a bare target="_blank", and don't open pages of the same app in a new tab (harness: link/new-tab-is-external).
Don't remove the underline (underline="none") where nothing else says it is a link, such as inside a paragraph.
Don't put a Link inside a clickable row, card or button: nested interactive elements can't be reached reliably.
a11y: Renders a native <a href> (or your router's link): Enter follows it, and it is announced and listed as a link.
Keyboard focus shows the 3px Focus/Accent ring, plus the underline for underline="hover".
external adds a visually hidden “(opens in a new tab)” to the name; the icon is decorative.
Inside text, colour alone must not mark a link (WCAG 1.4.1): underline it.
Inline links in a sentence are exempt from the 24×24 target size (WCAG 2.5.8); standalone links need room around them.
content: Name the destination in sentence case; no punctuation inside the link.
Front-load the key words (“Pricing plans”, not “Click to see our pricing plans”).
Don't type “(opens in a new tab)” yourself: external adds it.
refs: NN/g — Opening links in new browser windows and tabs

rules.summary: A Link goes somewhere: give it href, or a router link through `as` (+ `to`). An action on the page is a Button.
Link text names the destination on its own (“Billing settings”), never “click here”, “here”, “read more” or “learn more”.
A link that opens a new tab uses `external` (icon + hidden “(opens in a new tab)” + rel), not a bare target="_blank".
A tone="inherit" link keeps its default underline (always): in the text's own colour the underline is the only cue.

menu.title: Menu
menu.purpose: A button that opens a list of actions for an object: row actions in a table, a card's ⋯, an Edit or New menu. It uses the Popover surface and Popover/Item rows, follows the WAI-ARIA menu button pattern and floats in the overlay layer.
use: Secondary actions on an object that don't fit as buttons (Rename, Duplicate, Move to…, Delete).
Row actions in a Table (TableActions) and a Card's Sub-Action.
A menu button in a toolbar or page header (Edit, Share, New) that groups related commands.
avoid: Choosing a value (sort order, status, assignee) → SelectField, Segmented or Chip variant="advanced" + Popover.
Moving between pages → Sidebar, Tabs or Link.
One or two actions → show them as buttons.
A long or titled list of actions on a phone → BottomSheet type="action".
Forms or rich content → Dialog or SidePanel.
api: 240px, 4px padding, Large radius, Effect/Popover; portalled (or inside a [data-zen-overlay-root] device frame), 4px from the trigger, flips when there is no room
an IconButton whose aria-label names the object, or a Button; it gets aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded and aria-controls
items[] {id, label, icon, caption, shortcut, danger, disabled, onSelect} · { type: "separator" } · { type: "group", label, items }
or compose MenuItem / MenuSeparator / MenuGroup children
role=menuitem rows (PopoverItem itemRole="menuitem"); icon = an icon name (20px) or any element
Content/Negative text and icon; last, after a separator
start (default) · end (a trigger at the right end of a row or card)
uncontrolled and closed by default; a choice, Escape, Tab and an outside press close it
keyboard: On the trigger: open the menu on the first item
On the trigger: open the menu on the last item
Next item that starts with the typed letters
Run the focused item and close
Close and return focus to the trigger
Close and move on from the trigger
do: Name an icon-only trigger after its object, aria-label="Actions for INV-1042"; the name also labels the menu.
Start labels with a verb and keep them to 1–3 words; end with “…” only when the action asks for more input (Move to…).
Group related actions under MenuGroup headings or between separators; put destructive actions last, marked danger.
Keep an action that is unavailable right now visible but disabled, with a caption that says why.
Use align="end" when the trigger sits at the right end of a row or card.
Confirm a destructive choice in a negative Dialog, or offer Undo, after the menu closes; focus returns to the trigger.
Put menus straight into Table rows and Cards: the menu floats in the overlay layer, so overflow never clips it.
On a phone, keep menus to a few short actions; longer lists, or ones that need a title, are an Action BottomSheet.
dont: Don't use a Menu to pick a value or show a checked state; that is SelectField, Segmented or a Chip + Popover (harness: menu/not-for-selection).
Don't render a Menu without a trigger (harness: menu/needs-trigger), and don't open it on hover.
Don't put inputs, toggles or several lines of text inside menu items.
Don't open a menu from a menu item; open a Dialog or SidePanel for the next step.
Don't hide the one action people use most behind ⋯; show it as a button.
Don't mix items with and without icons in one menu.
a11y: Trigger: aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded and aria-controls; Enter, Space or ↓ open on the first item, ↑ on the last. A pointer opens the menu with focus on the menu itself.
role=menu labelled by its trigger; rows are role=menuitem (no aria-selected) with roving focus: ↑/↓ wrap, Home/End, typeahead.

Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger (a Dialog around it stays open); Tab closes and moves on from the trigger; choosing runs the item, closes and returns focus to the trigger unless the action moved it.
Disabled items are skipped by the arrow keys; their caption explains why.
Danger is never colour alone: the label says Delete or Remove.
content: Verb first, sentence case, 1–3 words (“Duplicate”, “Move to…”, “Delete invoice”).
Name the object once, in the trigger's aria-label, not in every item.
Shortcuts are hints in the platform's notation (⌘D, Ctrl+D); wire them in the app.

rules.summary: Icon names must exist (1,598 names that follow the Figma layer path, e.g. icon-search-medium-line); search them instead of guessing (MCP search_icons, or the Iconography page).
A Menu runs actions. Choosing a value (a selected or checked item) is a SelectField, a Segmented or a Chip + Popover.
A Menu has a trigger: a Button, or an IconButton whose aria-label names the object (“Actions for INV-1042”).

Every interaction a Zen control offers works: no no-op handlers (`() => {}`, `() => undefined`), which leave a field that ignores typing and ↑/↓ or a Dismiss that stays. Chat has chat/no-locked-interaction.

A controlled prop comes with its change handler (month + onMonthChange, value + onValueChange, open + onOpenChange, pageSize + onPageSizeChange…): without it nothing can change the value and the control is frozen, e.g. a DatePicker whose Previous/Next do nothing. Bare booleans (a fixed preview) and `x ? true : undefined` pins pass.

Screens, examples and templates (apps too since 2026-10-07; component source is skipped): every action does something when pressed. Flags a `Button` or `<button>` without onClick / href / type="submit" (IconButton: icon-button/needs-action), an action object ({ icon, label }) in leading, trailing, action, primaryAction, secondaryAction, subAction or actions without onClick, and pressable items whose list has no onSelect / onNavigate / onItemClick / onValueChange. Documented defaults pass: Dialog, ModalForm, SidePanel and BottomSheet actions close the overlay; a Menu opens from its trigger. Apps are not judged.

provider.title: ZenProvider (app root)
provider.purpose: The root of every Zen UI. It sets the token modes (data-theme, data-density…), paints the page Canvas and text colour, and hosts the portal that overlays render into, so dialogs, toasts and menus follow the same modes.
use: Wrapping the whole app once, right under React's root.
Switching a region to another mode (a dark hero, a mobile preview) with a nested provider.
Following the OS colour scheme with theme="system".
Following the OS Increase Contrast setting with contrast="system".
avoid: Styling a single component differently → its own props (level, size, theme).
Setting data-* attributes by hand → pass them as ZenProvider props.
Painting a card or panel → Card, Box or a Surface token; ZenProvider paints Canvas (the page).
api: neutral-s1 (default) · neutral-s2 · neutral-s3 · neutral-s4 · neutral-s5 · neutral-s6 · neutral-s7 · brand-s1 · brand-s2
auto (default on the root: < 744 mobile, < 1024 tablet) · desktop · tablet · mobile
dashboard (default, web apps) · mobile (phone apps) · popular (marketing)
standard (default) · high (Zen-High-Contrast: Subtle borders 3:1, placeholder and Light text 4.5:1; step 9 and backgrounds keep their colour) · system (follows prefers-contrast: more)
BCP 47 (built in: en, vi): sets lang, date formats and every component's built-in text (aria-labels, Close, Next page, toolbar names); labels overrides single strings or adds a language
paint Canvas + text (default on) · write the modes on <html> (default for the outermost painting provider) · own portal root (default on) · root element
do: Wrap the app in exactly one root ZenProvider and import "@zen/design-system/styles.css" once.
Build phone apps with typography="mobile" (and density="comfortable" when targets are touch-first).
Offer light/dark with theme="system" or a toggle that sets theme; never hard-code dark colours.
Nest a provider to switch a region's mode; unset props inherit from the parent.
Render overlays (Dialog, Toast, Menu…) anywhere inside the provider: they portal into its root and keep its modes.

Set locale="vi" (or your app's language) once on the root: every Zen component's built-in text follows it; override single strings with labels={{ … }} and use a component's own prop (closeLabel, placeholder, aria-label) only for one-off wording.
dont: Don't set data-theme or data-density on elements by hand, or paint the page background yourself.
Don't wrap every component in its own provider; one root plus the few regions that really switch modes.
Don't give a nested provider paint when it only changes typography or density inside a card; pass paint={false}.
a11y: locale sets the lang attribute, so screen readers pronounce the content in the right language, and translates the accessible names Zen components give their icon-only controls.
theme="system" respects the user's OS setting; color-scheme is set so native controls and scrollbars match.

contrast="system" turns on Zen-High-Contrast when the OS asks for more contrast (Increase Contrast): Checkbox, Radio and Subtle control borders reach 3:1, placeholders and Light text 4.5:1. Text on Solid colour fills keeps its colours, so an Avatar's initials still need a readable name next to them.

description-list.title: Description List
description-list.purpose: Shows read-only term → value pairs in a semantic dl: order summaries and receipts, contact and profile details, specs and metadata.
use: Order summaries, receipts and invoices, closed by one total row (emphasis).
Contact, profile and account details, each row with an optional Edit or Copy action.
Product specs and record metadata (IDs, dates, owners) in Cards, Side Panels and Bottom Sheets.
avoid: Records people compare, sort or select → Table.
Rows people open or navigate to → List + ListItem.
Editable forms → labelled fields (InputField, SelectField…); turn one row into a field only for a quick inline edit.
One key number → Metric / MetricCard.
api: inline (default: term at the start, value at the end; stacks by itself under stackBelow) · stacked (term above value)
px of the list's own width; default 280, so lists in phone cards and sheets stay inline; 0 never stacks
rules between rows, Padding/Small on both sides; never above the first or below the last row
the total row: one per list, a High rule above it
a Tertiary sm Button or a Flat sm IconButton; it takes room only in its own row (like an iOS accessory), so rows without one keep their value on the end edge
items[] {id?, term, description, action?, emphasis?} · <DescriptionItem> children
do: Keep one end edge (user, 2026-10-04 / 10-06): every row ends on the list's end edge. A row action sits Gap/XSmall (8px) after its own value and takes room only in its row, as an iOS value cell with an accessory and Figma's Item (Content · Action): a row without an action keeps its value on the edge, so Copy on one DNS value next to Type and Host is fine. A Flat icon action lines its icon, not its 32px box, up with the edge. Amounts that add up to a total take no row actions (they must share one edge with the total): a one-off action there (remove a discount) is a removable Badge beside the term.
Use inline for short values (amounts, dates, statuses) and layout="stacked" for long ones (addresses, emails, notes).
Format every value for people: currency with its symbol, dates written out ("2 October 2026"), IDs as users see them.
Close a calculation with one emphasis row, the total; the rows above it stay regular (harness: description-list/one-emphasis).
Keep terms short nouns in a stable order across screens (Subtotal, Shipping, Tax, Total).
Name row actions with their row: `Edit<VisuallyHidden> email</VisuallyHidden>` or `aria-label="Copy order number"`.
Put the list inside a Card, Side Panel or Bottom Sheet body; it takes the container's width and stacks on its own when narrow.
dont: Don't use it for data people scan across records or sort; use a Table.
Don't emphasise more than one row, or colour values beyond a status (a positive discount, a negative balance).
Don't add Divider elements inside the list; use divider (a dl only holds dt/dd groups).
Don't give a row more than one action, or a Primary button.
Don't truncate values; long values wrap, or use layout="stacked".
a11y: Renders a native dl with each dt/dd pair grouped in a div, so screen readers announce every term with its value.
A row action sits in its own dd after the value; give it a name that includes the term.
Announce copy and inline-edit results with a VisuallyHidden role="status" region.
Never rely on colour alone: a discount keeps its minus sign, a status keeps its text.
content: Terms are sentence-case nouns without colons ("Shipping address", not "Shipping Address:").
Write "Free" or "None" when a value is legitimately empty; never leave it blank or use a dash.

rules.summary: One emphasised row per list: the total that closes the calculation.

action-bar.title: Action Bar
action-bar.purpose: The footer bar that holds a screen's main actions: the mobile footer CTA (Large, full width, Primary on top), the phone dual footer (Large Tertiary · Primary side by side) and the sticky action row of desktop detail and edit pages (Tertiary · Primary at the end).
use: Phone screens whose main action must stay reachable while the content scrolls (Add to cart, Continue, Place order).
Desktop edit and detail pages: Save changes / Undo changes next to an unsaved-changes status.
A running total or selection count next to the action that uses it (summary).
avoid: Actions of a Dialog, Side Panel or Bottom Sheet → their own primaryAction / secondaryAction footer.
App destinations → Bottom Navigation.
Actions on selected rows → Popover/Bulk-Action.
One button under a short form → a plain Button row after the fields.
api: vertical (default: Large full-width buttons, Primary on top) · horizontal (Tertiary · Primary side by side: on a phone or any bar under 480px the summary takes its own row and two Large buttons split the next one, the Bottom-Sheet dual footer; on desktop the summary sits at the start and Medium buttons at the end)
sticky (default: pinned to the bottom of the scroll area, settles at the end) · fixed (viewport; an in-flow spacer keeps the end reachable) · static
default (Surface/Default + Pale top rule) · alt (Surface/Alt) · none; never a drop shadow
{ label, onClick, level?, disabled?, startIcon?, type?, form? }: sized (lg vertical and on a phone-width horizontal bar, md on a wider horizontal bar) and ordered for you
Buttons in visual order: Primary first when vertical, last when horizontal
a total, selection count or status line; wrap text that changes in role="status"
bottom padding = max(Padding/Small, --zen-safe-area-bottom or env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + Padding/XSmall)
keyboard: Move through the actions in visual order (Primary first when vertical, last when horizontal)
do: Hold one Primary, the screen's main action (harness: action-bar/one-primary).

On phones pick the direction by the actions: vertical when one main action leads (Add to cart, with Save for later below: Large full-width, Primary on top); horizontal when the two are a pair people choose between (Clear all · Show 6 prints, Decline · Accept: two Large buttons, Primary at the end) (harness: action-bar/full-width-size, action-bar/primary-order).
Prefer primaryAction / secondaryAction: they get the right size and order in both directions, so one set of actions serves phone and desktop.
Place a sticky bar as the last child of the scrolling content, inside the form it submits (type: "submit").
Say what the actions act on in the summary ("2 prints · $96.00", "3 unsaved changes") and announce changes with role="status".
Disable the Primary only while its precondition is unmet, and say why in the summary ("No changes to save yet").
dont: Don't put two Primary buttons in the bar, or a Secondary as the alternative.
Don't use small buttons (2xs · xs · sm) in a vertical bar; stretched thin buttons read as fields.
Don't add a drop shadow or a tinted fill; the Pale top rule separates the bar.
Don't stack more than two actions on a phone; move the rest into the page or a More menu.
Don't use surface="none" on a sticky or fixed bar; the content would scroll visibly under the buttons.
Don't pad the page for the home indicator yourself; the bar already clears the safe area.
a11y: Buttons keep their visual order in the DOM, so Tab follows what people see; primaryAction / secondaryAction are reordered per direction.
With aria-label ("Order actions") the bar is a named group; without one it adds no extra landmark.
Announce summary changes (added to cart, saved) with role="status".
A sticky bar stays below open popovers (z-index 3 vs. 4), so a dropdown near the bottom opens over it.
content: Labels name the outcome with a verb: "Add to cart", "Save changes", "Place order · $86.40"; never "OK" or "Submit".
The Tertiary is a real alternative ("Save for later", "Undo changes"), not a second way to do the Primary.

rules.summary: An Action Bar holds one Primary, the screen's main action; everything else is Tertiary (or Danger when irreversible).
Button children follow the visual order: Primary first (on top) in a vertical bar, last (at the end) in a horizontal one. primaryAction / secondaryAction are ordered for you.
A vertical Action Bar stretches its buttons across the width, so they are size lg (the mobile footer CTA), never 2xs · xs · sm.

Screens, examples and templates (apps too since 2026-10-07; component source is skipped): every action does something when pressed. Flags a `Button` or `<button>` without onClick / href / type="submit" (IconButton: icon-button/needs-action), an action object ({ icon, label }) in leading, trailing, action, primaryAction, secondaryAction, subAction or actions without onClick, and pressable items whose list has no onSelect / onNavigate / onItemClick / onValueChange. Documented defaults pass: Dialog, ModalForm, SidePanel and BottomSheet actions close the overlay; a Menu opens from its trigger. Apps are not judged.

image.title: Image & Thumbnail
image.purpose: Shows a picture in a ratio frame that keeps its size while loading (Skeleton) and fails gracefully (neutral placeholder, alt kept). Thumbnail is the fixed square for list rows, tables and pickers.
use: Product, listing and article photos in cards and detail pages (Image with a ratio).
Galleries and feeds, with a caption (figure/figcaption) when the picture needs a credit or context.
Pictures in ListItem leading slots, Table media cells and pickers (Thumbnail on the Image-Size scale).
avoid: People → Avatar (initials fallback, status, stacks).
App or category symbols → DockIcon or Icon.
File types → FileIcon.
Decorative backgrounds → CSS on the container.
api: 1:1 · 4:3 · 3:2 · 16:9 · 3:4 or width ÷ height; unset = the picture's own ratio (4:3 while loading)
cover (default, crops) · contain (the whole picture on Neutral/Pale)
lazy (default) · eager for the first picture on screen
undefined → Skeleton; a load error → placeholder with icon-image-line, alt stays its name
rounded (radius steps with the size, like Avatar Square) · circle · square
do: Always pass alt: what the picture shows in context; alt="" only when it is decorative or text beside it names it (harness: image/needs-alt).
Set ratio so the frame keeps its size while loading and nothing jumps when the picture arrives.
Use loading="eager" only for the first picture on screen; keep the rest lazy.
Use Thumbnail md (40) in ListItem leading slots, sm (32) in captioned Table cells and xs (24) in plain ones.
When a picture fails, keep the frame and offer a way forward nearby (Try again, Replace).
Use fit="contain" for logos, documents and cut-outs that must not be cropped.
dont: Don't use a file name or "image of…" as alt (harness: image/alt-describes).
Don't repeat the caption or the row title in alt; screen readers would read it twice.
Don't size a picture with a fixed width and height; give it a ratio and let it fill its container.
Don't use Thumbnail for people; Avatar has initials, status and stacks.
Don't put text over a picture without a scrim or an overlay type that keeps it readable.
a11y: Image renders a native img (a figure with figcaption when captioned); alt is required by the type.
The loading Skeleton is aria-hidden; a failed picture's placeholder is role="img" named by alt (hidden when alt="").
A Thumbnail inside a button (a gallery strip) takes its name from the button: alt="" on the Thumbnail, aria-label and aria-pressed on the button.
content: Alt text is one short, specific sentence ("White houses and a windmill by the sea"), without "image of".
Captions add what the picture can't: place, credit, size ("Bridge at dusk · 50 × 40 cm print").
refs: W3C WAI — An alt decision tree

rules.summary: Write radius alone when the corners match, and set radiusTopLeft/TopRight/BottomRight/BottomLeft only where they differ from radius (Image's radius defaults to md).
radius="full" takes no finite corner (radiusTopLeft/TopRight/BottomRight/BottomLeft other than full or none): use one token for all corners, or a finite radius with corner overrides.
Image and Thumbnail always carry alt: what the picture shows, or alt="" when it is decorative or the text beside it already names it.
alt describes the picture in context: never a file name, and never "image of…" / "photo of…" (screen readers already announce an image).

visually-hidden.title: Visually Hidden
visually-hidden.purpose: Adds text that only assistive technology reads: names for icon-only table headers, context for repeated links, status announcements, hidden headings and skip links that appear on focus.
use: Column headers that show only an icon or nothing (Actions, Starred).
Context that makes repeated labels unique ("Read more about …", "Edit email").
Status messages for changes shown only visually (role="status": "Link copied to the clipboard").
Skip links (as="a" + focusable) and headings that name a region for screen-reader navigation.
avoid: Naming an icon-only button → IconButton aria-label (it also shows the name as a tooltip).
Naming a field → its label, or aria-label when the context labels it.
Hiding content from everyone → don't render it.
Hiding decoration from screen readers → aria-hidden.
api: span (default, inline) · div · p · label · legend · a · h1–h6
shows the content while it, or a link inside it, has focus: a Surface pill at the top-start corner (skip links)
role="status" for announcements; id for aria-labelledby / aria-describedby
keyboard: Follow the skip link; focus moves to the main content
do: Start hidden text that continues a visible label with a space and no punctuation (`Edit<VisuallyHidden> email</VisuallyHidden>`) so the name reads as one phrase.
Render a status region from the start, empty, then change its text; a region inserted together with its message is often not announced.
Make the skip link the first focusable element of the page and point it at the main content (`tabIndex={-1}`).
Keep the visible label inside the accessible name (WCAG 2.5.3): add words, never replace them.
dont: Don't hide a link or control without focusable; keyboard users would land on something invisible (harness: visually-hidden/focusable-shows).
Don't stuff keywords or long instructions into hidden text; screen-reader users hear every word.
Don't use display:none, visibility:hidden or the hidden attribute for screen-reader text; they remove it from the accessibility tree.
Don't hide a heading sighted people need too; show it.
a11y: The text is clipped to a 1px box (clip-path) and taken out of the flow, but stays in the accessibility tree and in-page search.
Browsers insert a space before out-of-flow text when they build a name, so begin the hidden part with a space.
A focused skip link shows a Surface pill with a Subtle ring and the Focus/Accent outline (WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks, 2.4.7 Focus Visible).
content: Write hidden text as it will be heard: "Actions", " about Choosing a paper for photo prints", "Link copied to the clipboard".
